mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stop falling and begin to recover from their current depressed levels, weekday footfall should translate into higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks because commuting restores store visits near job and station clusters.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below the last 4-week mean even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT each rise for four consecutive weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays above baseline and does not release into outside activity, retail trips are pulled down within one week because discretionary outings are substituted by staying home, lowering RETAIL_REC immediately.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above +20 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its prior-week value after RESIDENTIAL stays above +20 for two straight weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM falls faster than TRANSIT, the same household urgency that reduces one errand channel also suppresses adjacent retail trips, so RETAIL_REC declines over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days while GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT both remain below their current weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS mobility spikes relative to the recent baseline, that shift indicates substitution toward outdoor recreation and away from shopping districts, which should reduce RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -20 after having been below -25 for at least two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall below the last 4-week mean after PARKS crosses above -20 from a prior two-week sub -25 regime.

mechanism_narrative: A synchronized rise in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES creates a commuting-and-lunching pattern that lifts nearby retail visits within two weeks, so RETAIL_REC should move up when both series improve together.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays flat or declines over 14 days despite simultaneous week-on-week increases in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS and RESIDENTIAL stay elevated while WORKPLACES remain weak, weekend substitution dominates and retail spending shifts away from stores, producing lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its trailing 4-week mean even though PARKS and RESIDENTIAL stay above current levels while WORKPLACES do not recover.

mechanism_narrative: In a renewed restriction regime, the current combination of low TRANSIT and WORKPLACES locks in suppressed shopping trips, so RETAIL_REC should keep drifting lower over the next week before any broader recovery can appear.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -70 and WORKPLACES stays below -55 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases in the next 7 days despite TRANSIT remaining below -70 and WORKPLACES remaining below -55.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in GROCERY_PHARM after a multi-week drop signals renewed out-of-home errand activity that spills into nearby retail visits, so RETAIL_REC should improve over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises by at least 5 points week-on-week after two declining weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase over the next 14 days after GROCERY_PHARM posts a week-on-week rise of at least 5 points following two down weeks.
